headline: Perturbation responses separate intrinsic from latent criticality in spiking populations
label: Constraints On Neural Dynamics
summary: Perturbation-response measures, energy-state-dependent excitability, and low-dimensional EEG models now probe which constraints shape neural dynamics.
synthesis: The dominant thread is identifying which constraints determine the dynamical regimes of neural populations, with three preprints approaching this from different levels. Perturbation-response measurements are proposed to distinguish intrinsic criticality from correlations driven by latent inputs in spiking neural populations. A Brian2 simulation of a 5,000-neuron gLIF network examines how Q10 metabolic scaling alters excitability, STDP and synchrony across energy states, linking cellular energetics to plasticity. A two-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck numerical twin with interpretable parameters reproduces transient EEG spindle bursts under anesthesia. What is new is the explicit separation of intrinsic from latent sources of criticality, the treatment of energy state as a control on plasticity and synchrony, and a low-dimensional stochastic model of transient oscillations.
